startup.name: Derya
startup.description: Supply chain automations that run a customer's supply chain function from prospecting and procurement to distribution of goods, for startups, SMEs and enterprises in robotics, commodities and food and beverage. Derya procures goods and manages operations for them. Two people, San Francisco, Summer 2026.

yc_acceptance.basis: Blind test: the company is already accepted to YC for its batch, so the acceptance estimate is a placeholder near certainty rather than a forecast. The unconditional prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent, third party figures in yc_acceptance.md).
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable in this test because the company was accepted. Had it been assessed as an applicant, the most plausible reason for a no would be a broad pitch with a brokerage model that investors may see as low margin. The founders would also need to show in the interview that they can ship quickly and have a specific first customer in mind, since YC weighs team speed and clear user need over market size.

ladder.why_it_fails: The likely stopper is that the pitch is too broad. Procurement, prospecting and distribution across robotics, commodities and food is three businesses, and investors want one wedge with margin. Mentum raised a 4.2M seed with a focused procurement assistant, while Alima raised 1.5M in food supply and then went inactive, which shows the risk of the food side.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Near the 22 percent anchor, set at 0.9x: a company that moves goods and takes margin can show revenue early, but gross margin per trade is thin.

The likely miss is that the company acts as a broker with low margins and working capital needs, so growth is capital hungry and investors see a trading business. Alima and Bulk MRO show how slow that can be.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B needs automation to lower cost per order across many customers. The likely stop is that incumbent platforms like Flexport, Zycus and Coupa add agents, and customers keep buying through relationships that agents do not replace. The analogs in the records suggest only a minority of companies in this cohort that reach a seed ever reach this round, and the company would need clear paying customers and improving margins to be among them.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C needs a platform for industrial trade with network effects. The likely end is a regional broker with low margins or an acquisition by a distributor or logistics company. The records show very few comparable companies reaching this stage, and those that did had durable revenue and a defensible position, which this company would need to show well before then.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stalls as a thin margin broker or pivots. Industrial trade runs on relationships and working capital, and agents reduce effort without owning the transaction. Alima went inactive and Mentum was acquired, while Arnata, with a narrower freight wedge, raised a 6.5M seed in 2023.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents for email, quoting and order handling are buildable by two people. The hard part is operations: payments, compliance and supplier trust across countries.

takeover_risk.rationale: Platforms can add agents quickly but moving goods and owning supplier relationships is operational work they avoid. A well resourced rival would need roughly the stated time and would have the incentive if the category proves valuable.

brand.rationale: Derya is short and easy to say and is a given name in some languages, which can sound friendly but does not signal industrial trade. It has little effect either way.

narrative.headline: A broad AI brokerage pitch with thin margins that needs one sharp wedge to raise beyond a small seed.
narrative.general_summary: Derya runs supply chain functions for customers using AI agents across robotics, commodities and food. The wedge is wide and brokerage margins are thin, which is why the seed is set a little below the B2B anchor. Analogs split: Mentum and Arnata raised seeds, Alima went inactive. Later steps follow the B2B anchors with a small discount for working capital needs, and a small acquisition is the likeliest exit. The estimates are anchored on the 2023 to 2025 B2B cohort and adjusted only with the stated reasons, keeping each step within 0.75 times its anchor. Reaching a later round years after the batch is common for companies with paying customers, and a pivot followed by a raise is part of the upside band, so the ladder asks whether a round is reached and not how fast.

assumptions: Customer and revenue facts were not given.

Blind test: only the batch input file and market web searches were used; no company specific records. The seed step is read as a round above the standard YC deal of about 500K dollars within roughly 12 months of batch start.

Extraction coverage is 662 of 6,399 companies researched in the calibration sample, plus recent cohort records; later cohorts are right censored, so base rates for 2023 to 2025 batches understate eventual progress.
